# First Working Day: Navigating the Platform

## 🗺️ Understanding the Layout

The noobly Wiki interface has three main areas:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Logo  🔍 Search Box     Profile  Help  Settings        │ ← Top Navigation
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Left Sidebar │                              │ Right     │
│              │                              │ Panel     │
│  Spaces      │   Main Content Area          │ (Chat &   │
│  └ Folders   │   (Document View)            │  Info)    │
│  └ Documents │                              │           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. **Top Navigation Bar**
- **Logo**: Click to return to home
- **Search Box**: Find documents across all spaces
- **Layout Switcher**: Change how you view content (Detailed, Content, Chat, Search)
- **Profile Icon**: Access your profile and settings
- **Help (?)**: Access help documentation
- **Settings**: Change app preferences

### 2. **Left Sidebar (Navigation Panel)**
- Lists all **Spaces** you have access to
- Click a space name to open it
- **Folders** appear below the space—click to browse
- **Breadcrumb trail** at the top shows: `Space > Folder > Subfolder`
- **Collapse/Expand** folders by clicking the arrow next to them

### 3. **Main Content Area**
Shows one of the following:
- **Document View**: Read and edit a document
- **Folder View**: List documents in a folder
- **Search Results**: Documents matching your search
- **Home Dashboard**: Welcome screen with recent and pinned documents

### 4. **Right Panel (Optional)**
- **Chat Assistant**: Ask questions and get answers
- **Document Info**: Metadata, last updated, author
- **Notes Panel**: Your personal annotations (if you open a document)

---

## 🗂️ Understanding Spaces

**Spaces** are the main organizational units in the noobly Wiki. Think of a space as a team, project, or business area.

### Examples of Spaces
- **Engineering**: Organization-wide documentation
- **Projects**: Active project files
- **Teams**: Team-specific knowledge
- **Architecture**: System designs and technical docs
- **Processes**: Workflow and procedure documentation

### Switching Between Spaces

1. Look at the **left sidebar**
2. Click on any **space name** to open it
3. The space's folders and documents will load below
4. The **breadcrumb** at the top updates to show your current space

### Space Permissions

Not all spaces are visible to everyone:
- **Public Spaces**: Anyone can view (but maybe not edit)
- **Team Spaces**: Only team members can view
- **Private Spaces**: Only specific people can view

If you don't see a space you need, ask your administrator for access.

---

## 📁 Navigating Folders

Folders organize documents within a space. They work like folders on your computer:

```
Engineering Space
├── Architecture
│   ├── System Design
│   ├── API Documentation
│   └── Database Design
├── Processes
│   ├── Onboarding
│   └── Change Management
└── Teams
    ├── Platform Team
    └── Data Team
```

### Exploring Folders

1. **Click a folder name** in the left sidebar to see its contents
2. **Expand/Collapse** a folder by clicking the arrow (▶/▼)
3. **Hover over a folder** to see options (more details, actions)
4. **Single-child folders** may appear collapsed (e.g., "Architecture › System Design") to save space

### Breadcrumb Trail

At the top of the main area, you'll see your path:
```
Engineering > Architecture > System Design
```
- Click any part to jump back to that level
- Use this to understand where you are in the hierarchy

---

## 📄 Viewing Documents

### Opening a Document

1. **Click the document title** in the left sidebar or folder view
2. The document loads in the main area
3. You'll see:
   - Document title
   - Author and last updated date
   - Tabs (Content, Blocks, Markdown, Visualize—depending on document type)
   - Comments and annotations section
   - Notes panel (right side)

### Document View Tabs

| Tab | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| **Content** | Clean, formatted reading view |
| **Blocks** | Edit structured content (if you have edit rights) |
| **Markdown** | Raw markdown (for technical editing) |
| **Visualize** | Diagram-based navigation (if document has layout) |

### Quick Actions on Documents

- **Print** or **Save as PDF**: Look for the browser print icon or menu
- **Share**: Click the share icon to copy a link or share with someone
- **Pin**: Save it to your pinned documents (star icon)
- **Search Within**: Use Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F on Mac) to find text on the page
- **Download**: Some documents (PDFs, files) have a download button

---

## 🔄 Different View Modes

Change how the platform displays content using the layout switcher (top toolbar):

### **Detailed View**
- Shows full sidebar with all spaces and folders
- Full breadcrumb and document context
- Best for: Exploring and understanding structure

### **Content View**
- Hides sidebar, focuses on reading
- Minimal distractions
- Best for: Reading long documents

### **Chat View**
- Document on the left, chat assistant on the right
- Ask questions about what you're reading
- Best for: Learning and research

### **Search View**
- Optimized for search results and filtering
- Shows results with preview
- Best for: Finding information

### **How to Switch**

1. Look for the **view switcher** in the top toolbar (looks like different layout icons)
2. Click the icon for your preferred view
3. The interface updates instantly
4. Your choice is remembered for next time

---

## 🔗 Breadcrumb Navigation

The **breadcrumb trail** shows where you are:

```
Home > Engineering > Architecture > System Design > Database Schema
```

- **Click any part** to jump to that level
- Helps you understand context and navigate back
- Always shows your path from the root

---

## 🚀 Quick Navigation Tips

### Use Keyboard Shortcuts
- **Ctrl+F** (Cmd+F on Mac): Search within current document
- **Ctrl+Home**: Jump to home
- **/?**: Show all keyboard shortcuts (if available)

### Use the Search Box
Instead of clicking through folders, just type in the **search box at the top** and find what you need in seconds.

### Bookmark Frequently-Used Documents
- **Pin documents** (star icon) to save them to your dashboard
- **Save search queries** to run them again later
- **Use browser bookmarks** for quick access

### Read Breadcrumbs
Always check the breadcrumb to understand where you are and navigate back to a parent folder.

---

## 📊 Folder Views

When you click on a folder, you can see its contents in different ways:

### **Grid View**
- Shows documents as cards with thumbnails
- Good for visual browsing
- See cover images and summaries at a glance

### **List View**
- Shows documents as a simple list
- Good for reading names and dates
- More compact than grid view

### **Details View**
- Shows documents with extra metadata
- Last updated, file type, size
- Good for scanning information

**Switch between views** using the view switcher in the toolbar (top-right of the main area).

---

## 🎯 Finding Your Way: Common Scenarios

### I want to explore everything in my team's space
1. Click your **team's space** in the left sidebar
2. Click a **folder** to see documents
3. Read through documents of interest
4. Use **breadcrumb** to navigate back

### I'm looking for something but not sure where
1. Use the **search box** at the top
2. Type a keyword
3. Browse results and click any to read it

### I want to go back to where I was
1. Use the **breadcrumb trail** at the top
2. Or use your **browser back button**
3. Or click the same space/folder again in the sidebar

### I'm lost
1. Click the **logo** at the top to go to home
2. Or click **Engineering** (or another main space) to reset
3. Or look at the breadcrumb to see where you are

---

## ⚙️ Customizing Your Navigation

### Collapsing/Expanding Spaces
- Click the **arrow** next to a space name to hide its folders
- Useful for cleaning up the sidebar if you have many spaces

### Reordering (if allowed)
- Some installations allow you to **drag and reorder** spaces and folders
- Check if this is available by trying to drag a space name

### Sidebar Width
- **Drag the right edge of the sidebar** to make it wider or narrower
- Helpful if you have long folder names

---

## ✅ Navigation Checklist

After this section, you should be able to:

- [ ] Identify the main areas of the interface (sidebar, main, right panel)
- [ ] Open a space and browse its folders
- [ ] Click on a document and read it
- [ ] Understand breadcrumb navigation
- [ ] Switch between different view modes
- [ ] Use the search box to find documents quickly

---

## 🆘 Troubleshooting Navigation

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Can't see a folder I expect | The folder might be empty or hidden. Check permissions or ask your team. |
| Sidebar is too narrow to read names | Drag the right edge of the sidebar to make it wider. |
| Document is taking too long to load | Try refreshing the page (F5). If it persists, check your internet connection. |
| Lost and can't remember where I was | Click the logo to go home, or look at the breadcrumb trail. |
| Can't switch between view modes | You might not have permission. Contact your administrator. |
